title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
excerpt: The opening minutes look genuinely cinematic. It's not just sharpness; it's the camera movement, depth and sense of scale.
body: I rented the HD version to watch on my TV. Within the opening minutes, what stood out wasn't the resolution at all: it was the way the film was shot. The camera movement feels deliberate and fluid, and the view from up on a building has a remarkable sense of height, clarity and space.
It's a kind of beauty you only notice when the images are moving. A good composition, a subtle move and the scale of the city can do more for me than an expensive action sequence.
This is just an opening impression, not my judgment of the film or its story. I'll rate it after watching the whole thing.

title: Slow Horses
excerpt: One of my clear favorites. A 9.5/10 sets a high bar for the shows that follow.
body: One of my favorite series, and the score reflects it. Very few shows make it into my personal 9.5/10 territory.
When I'm looking for another series, this is the sort of standard I have in mind. A personal favorite, not just something that's generally well-reviewed.

title: Legends
excerpt: The British series really worked for me. One of my stronger recent 9/10 watches.
body: I really liked this British series. That's the main point of the note: it earned a 9/10 from me.
I prefer to record a short opinion I actually hold than pad it into an invented review. More detail can come after a rewatch.

title: Your Friends & Neighbors
excerpt: A strong fit for my taste and one of my better recent watches.
body: I gave this 8.5/10. It worked well for me, enough to stand apart from the many series that I finish but don't feel strongly about.
For my personal list, it lands below the rare 9-plus favorites, but comfortably above the merely decent.

title: The Pitt
excerpt: I can understand why some see it as 9–10/10 television. For me, it's an 8.
body: This is a very good series. I can understand the case for an even higher score, but my personal enjoyment sits around 8/10.
That distinction matters: I can respect the quality of something without pretending I loved it more than I did.

title: Black Rabbit
excerpt: Good. I enjoyed it enough, but it doesn't quite reach my favorites.
body: My rating is 7.5/10. That's a positive score, but it doesn't mean I'm going to recommend it above the shows I rated 8.5 or 9.
I'm keeping the first entry brief rather than making up specific objections or praise I didn't record at the time.

title: Collateral
excerpt: Good, watchable, but not a standout.
body: A solid watch. I put it around 7/10: good, but not one of the series I'd single out as exceptional.
There's a big difference between being pleased that I watched something and wanting to tell everyone else to watch it. This is closer to the former.

title: The Gentlemen
excerpt: Entertaining enough. Somewhere around 6.5–7/10 for me.
body: I land around 6.5–7/10 on this one. It was fine, but it didn't deliver the sort of excitement or satisfaction that makes something a personal favorite.
Worth distinguishing from a bad show: it's just not especially high on my list.

title: The Beast in Me
excerpt: A strange watch, and not in a way that completely paid off for me.
body: Around 6/10. The word I kept coming back to was 'weird'.
I don't need every story to be conventional, but unusual choices still need to feel earned. This one didn't completely work for me.

title: Disclosure Day
excerpt: Watchable, but too formulaic and convenient. The ending held back exactly what I wanted to know.
body: It was good enough to pass the time, but I rated it around 6/10. A lot of it felt like familiar Hollywood machinery rather than an intelligent story whose characters behaved convincingly.
Too many convenient moments weakened the impact for me. And the ending withholding what the aliens actually said was particularly unsatisfying: it avoided the very answer I'd been waiting for.
A movie can be technically polished and still leave me feeling that the writing didn't do the premise justice.
